title: 👀 Wall Street gets a peak inside Anthropic
body_text: The Los Angeles Dodgers were favorites to win this year’s World Series. And when they were surprisingly swept by the Milwaukee Brewers, it wasn’t just the team that lost – businesses around Dodger stadium also saw potential revenue evaporate. Fortune reports that a restaurant group that runs bars near the stadium prepared for exactly that possibility by placing a $60,000 trade on Kalshi that the Dodgers would not advance. The trade, which doubled in value after LA’s playoff exit, helped to fill the hole in the group’s revenue from all the Dodger’s fans who now won’t be packing bars before or during World Series games. Investors have been eager to peek under the hood of Anthropic ahead of its anticipated Wall Street debut, which could value the AI company at around $2 trillion. The Wall Street Journal got their hands on an early draft of Anthropic’s hotly anticipated S-1 , which paints a picture of a company with surging revenues but also sky-high compute costs and a medley of risk factors. Here are some highlights : Revenue is growing at an impressive rate: It reported $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of this year, up from $1.1 billion in the same period a year earlier. They are also spending a ton of money on compute. The company spent $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, up from $2.3 billion spent on infrastructure during the same period in 2025. The company already agreed to pay $450 billion in cloud computing agreements over the next seven to ten years and it can’t back out of those. It warned it could potentially spend $750 billion “in the coming years,” per the Journal. It is in the red. The company reported a net loss of $80 billion during the first half of 2026, compared to a net loss of $13 billion a year earlier. Most of that loss is accounting charges; it still reported operating loss in H1 2026 but it was lower than the year before. Anthropic makes it very clear that it sees AI as a risky business. According to the Journal, “roughly a third” of the draft prospectus was dedicated to risk factors ranging from liability tied to potential data security incidents, models “blackmailing” people to the political risk tied to the backlash against data centers. The CEO isn’t getting a Musk-sized pay day. Dario Amodei’s total compensation is $18 million, which is in line with the median pay for S&P 500 companies but less than many of his Big Tech peers. Anthropic’s numbers scooped by the Journal give a rare glimpse at the precise economics of running an AI company. The good news is Anthropic’s revenue, as of June 30, is growing faster than its costs. The bad news is that its costs are really high. Anthropic needs to convince investors that its revenues are going to keep growing faster than its enormous spending commitments. But, as Bloomberg’s Parmy Olson recently pointed out , the price of building AI models keeps going up while the price tag on AI products keeps going down. Anthropic can't guarantee that its revenue will keep soaring, but it's already committed to paying hundreds of billions of dollars for computing power. “That doesn’t necessarily mean a bursting bubble, but it does look like the real power increasingly lies with the companies that distribute and power the technology: cloud giants like Microsoft Corp., Alphabet Inc. and Amazon .com Inc.,” Olson wrote. Amazon’s annual holiday hiring surge is set to be bigger than ever, the e-commerce giant has announced . The company says it will hire over 300,000 seasonal, part-time, and full-time new employees to deal with the increase in orders it sees during the holiday shopping season. The yield on 10-year French government bonds hit 5% on Wednesday , as the nation’s borrowing costs spiked amid mass unrest that has turned violent at times. Larry Ellison went on a borrowing spree to fund his son’s takeover of Warner Bros ., the Wall Street Journal reports . Wall Street stock strategists have a new favorite word . The average US mortgage rate fell for the first time in 2 months, dropping to 7.41% from 7.5% . Coca-Cola bought Costa coffee for $5 billion, hoping to create a global self-serve coffee behemoth. It didn’t end up that way, Bloomberg reports , largely because espresso machines are more complex than soda vending machines. Wearing a necktie can decrease blood flow to the brain by as much as 7.5%, a 2018 study found. Lockheed Martin , TTM Technologies , and Procter & Gamble slated to release earnings ahead of the open. title: 🤖 Meta has billions riding on its Muse
body_text: Usually you want a taco that has some varying texture. A woman in Texas is suing a regional taco chain, Torchy’s Tacos, for $250,000 after nearly swallowing a cow tooth. It’s not an uncommon thing to find in barbacoa, the kind of meat that filled her “Democrat” taco, which is slow cooked beef cheek. Still, the woman was “grossed out and sickened,” according to reports. Meta — one of the largest and spendiest companies in the artificial intelligence trade — is slated to report earnings today after the bell. The report comes at a time when investors are increasingly worried about the amount of debt companies are taking on to fuel their AI ambitions. Specifically, investors are worried that companies like Meta took on a dangerous amount of debt to create products that have not yet proven that they will generate enough revenue to pay that money back. Meta’s message to investors will likely be something along the lines of: “trust the process.” Meta up until recently had little to show for its AI spend, and is expected to report $41.1 billion in capital expenditures for the quarter and $9.4 billion negative free cash flows, which would mark its first cash flow negative quarter since 2012. While we're on the topic, here’s what else the Street is expecting: Revenue at $63.3 million, up 23% year over year. Adjusted earnings per share at $6.79, down 6.3% year over year. Meta unveiled Muse, its personal AI agent, on Sept 8, meaning we’ll get a peak at how the new product performed in the first few weeks. The app surpassed 5 million downloads in its first three weeks, according to Sensor Tower data cited by multiple outlets .Wall Street appeared hopeful, sending Meta rallying in the weeks after the launch. Muse, which has a furry mascot that’s equal parts cute and unsettling, is one of the first big consumer AI products. You give it the keys to your email and credit cards and it can do things that are the bane of our existence, like make dinner reservations or order more Tide Pods. That’s a bit of a different play than its peers, which have made big bets on AI as a tool for corporations eager to do more with less humans. The relationship between AI companies and corporations is starting to show cracks but its relationship with consumers over a subscription based service is still in its early innings. It’s ultimately unclear if Muse will be the cashcow it needs to be in order to justify the amount Meta has spent on AI. The economics of a subscription product is also very different to Meta’s lucrative advertising business. And, as my colleague Walter Hickey pointed out earlier, it takes AI competitors like Amazon being willing to play ball in order for this thing to work as advertised. As we wade into a big week for tech earnings, the questions on everybody’s mind is as follows: How much more money are you going to spend and or borrow? When is the thing you’re working on going to make money? In Meta’s case, it has a shiny new product to talk about which is a better position than most of its peers. While it very well may report positive early adoption data, it still has to prove the product will be worth the many billions of dollars spent on it. title: 🥤 Soda streaming wars
body_text: Who’s for a game of six degrees of sartorial separation? Kevin Bacon, whose name lends itself to a game where people have to connect Hollywood figures back to the “Footloose” star in as few steps as possible, now hopes to be linked up with something much dearer to him: a box of clothes from the ‘90s. In a video posted to Instagram, the 68-year-old actor detailed the worldwide journey that the clothes have been on via New York, Memphis, France, Germany, Israel, and England, seemingly calling out FedEx as the offending courier behind the weeks-long route. Bacon sent out the plea with hopes to be reunited with the “old boots, old jeans, and old hats” in his original intended delivery destination of Ireland, and a spokesperson from the delivery giant has since confirmed they are now in direct contact with Bacon’s team. Stocks rose on Monday as chipmakers bounced back from last week’s drubbing. When you imagine the prolonged talks and tense negotiations that are thrashed out between some of the biggest names in global business, you might not imagine rooms of execs and franchisees sipping samples of innovative new tinctures, but that’s apparently how it went down in Texas over a couple of days in June , as KFC prepared to decide on a drink supplier moving forward. The choice, as it has often been for companies and customers alike through the years, was simple: Coke or Pepsi ? Follow in the footsteps of McDonald’s, Burger King, Wendy’s and many more by partnering with the most recognizable beverage brand of all time, or stick with Pepsi, the company that spun the chicken chain off as part of Yum! Brands in 1997 and has provided its drinks selection since the original acquisition some 40 years ago? This time, the Yum! fast-food behemoth went for Coca-Cola, switching from Pepsi in a move that mirrors the American soda-loving population at large. According to figures shared with Snacks by industry insights and analysis company Beverage Digest, Pepsi’s share of the carbonated soft drink market in the US has fallen from just over 13.6% at the start of the twenty-first century, to a little over 8% as of last year. In that time, Coca-Cola’s share has slipped much more slightly, down from 20.2% in 2000, to a still-strong 18.5% in 2025. In addition, last year was the third in a row where Dr. Pepper has taken a bigger share of the market than Pepsi, with Sprite and Diet Coke now also not far behind, taking 7.9% and 8% of soda case sales in the US, respectively. While it’s not the end of the world for Pepsi — the drinks giant will maintain its partnerships with international branches of KFC — it’s still a big blow, as Coca-Cola extends its already dominant position in the soft-drink fountain game, where it currently accounts for 70% of sales by volume, per separate Beverage Digest data . The $15 million haul makes the film built around the imprisoned Theranos founder the biggest debut for a non-music or concert doc since 2004’s “Fahrenheit 9/11.” Tt’s also the largest opening for a movie showing on under 1,000 screens since “Borat” hit American cinemas in 2006, per Variety . The CEO of CoreWeave , which slumped almost 25% last week, has offloaded nearly $1 billion worth of shares since its IPO in March last year . Within 30 minutes of preorders opening, estimated delivery dates for Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo had shifted from October 23, 2026 to January 25, 2027, MacRumors reports . Elon Musk announced plans to give every American child a single share of SpaceX next year, amounting to around $10.5 billion worth of stock at its current valuation. Despite only recently rising to take second place in America’s soda wars, Dr Pepper is actually the oldest of America’s three most popular soft beverages. The vaguely-flavored “pepper soda” was first sold in 1885, one year before Coca-Cola and around eight years before Pepsi, or “ Brad’s Drink ” as it was then.
